as_told.title: Immaculate Constellation report: triangle ARVs over Indo-PACOM

plain: Slowly rotating triangles of light were seen over the waters watched by the US military's Indo-Pacific Command, says a researcher who goes by UAPGerb, who tells Michels on two shows that this comes from the Immaculate Constellation report, an unsigned paper entered into the record of a congressional hearing on 13 November 2024; the papers call themselves the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, a former Defense Department official named Matthew Brown later said he wrote it, and the department says it has no record of a program by that name. In one telling UAPGerb calls the triangles three-lighted "alien reproduction vehicles", craft built to copy alien ones, flown by an adversary over "Chinese territory", which would mean a rival power already flies such craft. The report describes a rotating equilateral triangle over "a grouping of vessels engaged in SIGINT and MASINT collection", ships gathering electronic and other technical intelligence, "at night in a specific area of the Pacific Ocean", expected "due to foreign pre-positioning of advanced collection assets", and in a second case calls the triangle "an ARV/RV of unknown origin", so the Chinese territory and the adversary are his reading, a step from words that place the ships in the Pacific, call the assets foreign and leave the craft's origin unknown.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report has two triangle cases under INDOPACOM: in one a slowly rotating equilateral triangle appears over "a grouping of vessels engaged in SIGINT and MASINT collection at night in a specific area of the Pacific Ocean", and the vessels are said to have expected it "due to foreign pre-positioning of advanced collection assets"; in the other the triangle is "an ARV/RV of unknown origin". UAPGerb's "Chinese territory" and "adversarial ARV" are his reading of these cases, a step from their words: the first places the ships in the Pacific and calls the collection assets foreign, and the second gives the craft's origin as unknown.
